source.oracle: test_source_oracle.py executes extracted pinned source methods and Python standard-library shlex; it does not import the product or the Rust implementation.

editor_source.history_api_correction: The requested new(capacity, None) is not a Reedline 0.52.1 API. new(capacity) explicitly initializes its private file field to None; only with_file accepts a path.
editor_source.typecheck_status: Primary-source signatures verified; Cargo all-target checks require the parent's dependency graph and serial validation slot.

intentional_differences: The owner selected Reedline rather than Python PromptSession. Plain escaped prompt layout is retained; Rich styling, blinking cursor, key bindings, multiline editing and history-search UI are not claimed identical.
EOF is a distinct StopReason::EndOfInput and stops after one event. The source inner Exception handler instead prints 'Error in interactive session: ' for EOFError and breaks without a farewell.
Actual stdin and stdout must both be terminals. Redirected streams are explicitly unsupported before creating Reedline; there is no pseudo-terminal or environment fallback.

Submitted line bytes, token count, prompt bytes and retained history payload are bounded. Oversized or malformed lines fail without truncation. Reedline live editing/undo allocation has no hard byte ceiling.
History is in-memory and capacity-bounded, unlike the source's unlimited InMemoryHistory. Reedline omits empty lines and consecutive duplicates.

There is no log-file-path emission, hidden singleton, global runtime-mode mutation, terminal styling, custom completer, SDK or authentication initialization in this component. The application owns mode, diagnostics and dispatch.

Handled application/parser failures are host-owned Continue outcomes; fatal host errors stop with RunError::Host. Lexical ValueError-equivalent failures terminate with RunError::Line as the source inner exception path does.
host_contract: Token/action fixtures use a parser fake accepting arbitrary first tokens so they test lexing and raw aliases, not actual command registration or acceptance.

The source catches SystemExit from a selected subparser's parse_args, but its unknown-command self.parser.error call is outside that catch and propagates SystemExit. The caller must distinguish handled subparser failures from fatal root command errors; this crate does not invent a command registry.
